REFERENCE-PRESERVING KINETIC PULSES AND FINITE ENTROPY INFERENCE
2026-10-31. Derived theorem and finite acquisition contract.

1. Target, interface and organizing construction

Let Q be an unknown finite irreducible all-even continuous-time Markov
generator, with stationary law pi and reciprocal edge support. Write
a_ij=pi_i q_ij. The target is the ZERO-FIELD STATIONARY MEAN entropy
production rate
 sigma_0=sum_{i<j} (a_ij-a_ji) log(a_ij/a_ji).
It is not realised entropy on the pulse, mean jump activity, maximum
escape rate, controlled-law identification or the entire device heat.
Stationary preparation and deterministic state labels are supplied.

A prescribed kinetic pulse has q^m_ij(t)=m_ij(t)q_ij off diagonal,
m_ij(t)=m_ji(t)>=0, and repaired diagonals. Its known dimensionless
amplitude envelope is m_ij(t)<=M(t). Define B=integral_0^T M(t)dt>0.
Q, pi, state count, mixing time and an escape-rate cap are not inputs.
The physical time T and amplitude envelope are inputs. Uniform
observed-label cut gating is one possible implementation, not an
operation whose microscopic qualification follows from two bits.

Construct a VIRTUAL reversible generator R by
 pi_i R_ij=sqrt(a_ij a_ji), i!=j,
and repair its diagonal. It is reversible with stationary law pi. Every
symmetric pulse R^m remains stationary at pi, even for a time-varying
prescribed symmetric protocol. This is the organizing fact: the
comparison law retains its initial measure during the full pulse.
R need never be fitted, implemented or observed.

2. Exact path relative entropy, including waiting terms

For two finite CTMCs started with the same pi, the log path-density ratio
is the sum of log jump-rate ratios minus the integral of escape-rate
differences. Under the reference R^m, the expected number of i->j jumps
per dt is pi_i m_ij R_ij dt. Thus
 D(P_(R^m)^pi || P_(Q^m)^pi)
 = integral sum_{i!=j} pi_i [m_ij R_ij log(R_ij/q_ij)
                              -m_ij R_ij+m_ij q_ij]dt.
For a reciprocal pair set a=a_ij, b=a_ji, c=sqrt(ab). Its logarithmic
terms cancel: c log(c/a)+c log(c/b)=0. The remaining pair contribution
is m_ij(a+b-2sqrt(ab)). In particular, with
 H=sum_{i<j}(sqrt(a_ij)-sqrt(a_ji))^2,

I’ll give a different research family a concrete test before choosing the next direction. I’ll start by retrieving N713’s governing source, then compare an autonomous geometric-control construction with the strongest continuation of the inference theory.

The strongest continuation I see is a finite experiment, not another population-identification layer: a bounded kinetic pulse, followed by one binary readout from each independently prepared system. I’m checking whether its finite-amplitude response can bound the original entropy-production rate without exact tables or a rank promise.

For the different-family test, I’ll construct a geometric quantum gate and compare its ideal holonomy with its finite-time operation. N713’s source-clock warning is directly relevant to that distinction.

The quantum construction is checked. A heralded clock can deliver the supplied unitary without knowing its absolute speed, but its mean completion time still scales as \(1/\lambda\). Splitting the bath’s logical channels also preserves the clock statistics while destroying the gate’s coherence. That route leaves the coherent gate interactions and detector supplied, so I’m not selecting it.

I’m choosing the finite kinetic-pulse experiment. The proof opening is a virtual reversible generator that stays stationary under symmetric rate changes. Comparing its path law with the real pulse may give a bound from finite endpoint probabilities, without reconstructing the hidden generator.

The remaining question is whether the pulse bound survives finite data at a useful cost. I’m checking that before collecting fresh simulated records, and keeping the independent preparations, calibrated pulse duration and symmetric gate as explicit resources.

The population calculation supports a concrete test: a reversible-looking binary signal gains a positive dissipation floor under a symmetric rate pulse. A simple witness appears sufficient to certify a floor of \(0.5\) nats per model-time unit from 32,768 independent preparations, with a matched equilibrium control and a power bound fixed before the draws. The source’s actual rate is about \(20.7\), so this would be a useful lower bound rather than close reconstruction.
